Class EffectTimer

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tfx.EffectTimer
public final class EffectTimer extends Object
Manages the timing and interpolation of effects.

The EffectTimer is responsible for:

  • Duration Tracking: Tracking total duration and remaining time
  • Progress Calculation: Computing alpha values (0.0 to 1.0) based on elapsed time
  • Easing Application: Applying interpolation functions for smooth animations
  • Direction Control: Supporting forward and reverse playback

Design Philosophy:

EffectTimer separates timing concerns from rendering logic. Effects use the timer's alpha() method to get a normalized progress value (0.0 to 1.0) that has been transformed by the interpolation function. This allows effects to focus on "what to render" rather than "when to render it."

Key Concepts:

  • Alpha Value: A normalized progress value (0.0 = start, 1.0 = end) that has been transformed by the interpolation function.
  • Interpolation: An easing function that transforms linear progress into smooth animation curves (e.g., ease-in, ease-out, bounce).
  • Overflow: When processing exceeds the timer's duration, the excess time is returned as overflow for use by subsequent effects in sequences.

Usage Pattern: 

EffectTimer timer = EffectTimer.fromMs(2000, Interpolation.SineInOut);

// In render loop
TFxDuration delta = TFxDuration.fromMillis(frameTimeMs);
TFxDuration overflow = timer.process(delta);

if (timer.done()) {
    // Effect complete
} else {
    float alpha = timer.alpha(); // Use alpha to drive effect
}

Reversing Effects:

Use reversed() to play an effect backwards, or mirrored() to reverse while preserving the visual curve shape (useful for ping-pong effects).

    • loopMode

      public EffectTimer loopMode(LoopMode mode)
      Sets the loop mode for this timer.

      Loop mode controls what happens when the timer completes:

      • LoopMode.ONCE: Timer completes and stays done (default)
      • LoopMode.LOOP: Timer resets to start and continues
      • LoopMode.PING_PONG: Timer reverses direction and continues
      Parameters:
      mode - the loop mode
      Returns:
      this timer for chaining

    • mirrored

      public EffectTimer mirrored()
      Returns a mirrored timer that runs in reverse direction with flipped interpolation.

      This preserves the visual curve shape when used with effects that reverse at construction time. Unlike reversed(), which flips both direction and interpolation type, mirrored() flips the interpolation to compensate for the reversed direction.

      Returns:
      a new timer with reversed direction and flipped interpolation

    • process

      public TFxDuration process(TFxDuration duration)
      Processes the timer by reducing the remaining duration by the specified amount.

      For looping timers, this method handles resetting or reversing the timer when it completes:

      • LoopMode.ONCE: Returns overflow when complete
      • LoopMode.LOOP: Resets to start, returns null
      • LoopMode.PING_PONG: Reverses direction, returns null
      Parameters:
      duration - The amount of time to process
      Returns:
      The overflow duration if the timer has completed (ONCE mode only), or null if still running

    • done

      public boolean done()
      Returns true if the timer has completed.

      For looping timers (LoopMode.LOOP and LoopMode.PING_PONG), this method always returns false since looping timers never complete on their own.

      Returns:
      true if the timer has completed
